new_entities.name: Levothyroxine for subclinical hypothyroidism in older adults
aliases: LT4 for older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism
new_entities.description: Levothyroxine treatment used in older adults with persistent subclinical hypothyroidism.

new_entities.name: Quality of life
new_entities.description: Health-related quality of life or sleep-related functional status measured with generic or disease-specific instruments.

edges.effect_quant: Across randomized evidence, levothyroxine has not meaningfully improved older adults' quality of life in subclinical hypothyroidism. The 21-study JAMA meta-analysis of 2,192 adults found no clinically relevant QoL or thyroid-symptom benefit, the 737-patient TRUST trial was negative on both ThyPRO primary outcomes, and the 80-plus pooled analysis in 251 participants again found no important quality-of-life gain.
edges.population: older adults with persistent subclinical hypothyroidism, especially community-dwelling adults aged 65 years and older
edges.mechanism: Correcting a mild biochemical thyroid deficit could theoretically improve fatigue, physical function, and health-related quality of life, but age-related symptom burden is often multifactorial and may not be driven primarily by thyroid hormone deficiency.
edges.summary: This is a fairly settled mixed-to-null edge. The best modern trials do not show clinically important quality-of-life improvement from routine levothyroxine treatment in older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism.
edges.caveats: These results do not exclude benefit in selected patients with more marked TSH elevation, clear hypothyroid symptoms, or specific comorbid contexts. The evidence mainly argues against routine symptom-directed treatment of the average older adult with mild SCH.

evidence.citation: StottDJ et al 2017 N Engl J Med
